questions.q: What is the general category of commercial tools this lesson discusses?
options: Dedicated products for continuous SQL Server monitoring and alerting, such as SolarWinds SQL Sentry, Redgate SQL Monitor, and Idera SQL Diagnostic Manager
Backup and restore utilities only
Free, built-in SQL Server system stored procedures
Antivirus software for database servers
questions.explain: The lesson names this category as commercial SQL Server monitoring products, giving SolarWinds SQL Sentry, Redgate SQL Monitor, and Idera SQL Diagnostic Manager as well-known examples.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what do commercial monitoring tools generally add on top of the DIY DMV-querying approach?
options: Continuous historical collection already graphed, built-in tunable alerting, and fleet-wide views across many instances
The ability to run T-SQL for the first time — DMVs are otherwise inaccessible
A replacement for SQL Server itself
Guaranteed elimination of all performance problems
questions.explain: The lesson describes the typical value-add as pre-built continuous collection and dashboards, built-in alerting, and fleet-wide views — not new underlying data sources.

questions.q: What real tradeoff does this lesson point out about adopting a commercial monitoring tool?
options: A real licensing cost, plus one more piece of infrastructure to install, patch, and secure
There is no tradeoff — these tools are entirely free and require no maintenance
Commercial tools cannot query DMVs at all
Adopting one guarantees you no longer need any DBA on staff
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that these products carry licensing cost and become another maintained piece of infrastructure, not a free or zero-effort addition.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why doesn't a commercial monitoring dashboard by itself fully solve a performance problem?
options: A dashboard surfaces what's happening, but a DBA still needs to understand the underlying fundamentals (like what a wait type actually means) to know what to do about it
Dashboards are always inaccurate
Commercial tools cannot display wait statistics
Dashboards only work with Azure SQL Database
questions.explain: The lesson stresses that a tool surfacing a problem is only useful to someone who already knows what the underlying metric means and how to respond.

questions.q: What does 'anomaly detection,' as mentioned in this lesson, generally refer to in a monitoring tool's alerting?
options: Alerting based on deviation from a server's own historical pattern, similar in idea to the baseline-comparison approach from the previous lesson
Detecting malware on the SQL Server host
Automatically rewriting slow queries without DBA review
A fixed threshold that never changes regardless of workload
questions.explain: The lesson connects commercial tools' adaptive alerting to the same idea introduced in the previous lesson: comparing against a server's own historical pattern rather than one static number.
